ChatGPT said:

You're essentially building a multi-tenant NFC card management platform. Here's how you can structure it using Node.js, Express, Handlebars, and a database (MongoDB or PostgreSQL recommended):

🧱 Core Components

  1. User Authentication System

    • Register/Login/Logout

    • Password hashing (bcrypt)

    • Session management (express-session)

  2. Card Management

    • Each card has a unique ID (printed or programmed into the NFC chip)

    • Cards are assigned to a user upon purchase

    • Users can configure their card's redirect URL

  3. Analytics Tracker

    • Log each card tap: timestamp, device IP, maybe geolocation

    • Store these analytics per card

  4. Dashboard

    • Shows user's cards and their analytics

    • Allow user to edit their redirect links

🗂 Database Schema Example (MongoDB style)

js
User {
  _id,
  email,
  passwordHash,
  name,
  cards: [CardID]
}

Card {
  _id,
  cardUID,         // Unique NFC ID
  owner: UserID,
  redirectUrl: String,
  analytics: [AnalyticsID]
}

Analytics {
  _id,
  cardId,
  timestamp,
  ipAddress,
  userAgent
}

🛠 Route Flow

  1. NFC Tap Route (Public)

    js
    app.get('/tap/:cardUID', async (req, res) => {
  const card = await Card.findOne({ cardUID: req.params.cardUID });
  if (!card) return res.status(404).send('Card not found');

  // Log analytics
  await Analytics.create({
    cardId: card._id,
    timestamp: new Date(),
    ipAddress: req.ip,
    userAgent: req.headers['user-agent']
  });

  res.redirect(card.redirectUrl);
});

  2. User Dashboard (Private)

    js
    app.get('/dashboard', isAuthenticated, async (req, res) => {
  const user = await User.findById(req.session.userID).populate('cards');
  res.render('dashboard', { user });
});

  3. Update Redirect URL

    js
    app.post('/card/:cardUID/edit', isAuthenticated, async (req, res) => {
  const card = await Card.findOne({ cardUID: req.params.cardUID, owner: req.session.userID });
  if (!card) return res.status(403).send('Unauthorized');

  card.redirectUrl = req.body.redirectUrl;
  await card.save();
  res.redirect('/dashboard');
});

📊 Analytics View

Use Chart.js or similar in your Handlebars template to show visual graphs:

html
<canvas id="cardAnalytics"></canvas>
<script>
const ctx = document.getElementById('cardAnalytics');
new Chart(ctx, {
  type: 'line',
  data: {
    labels: {{analytics.timestamps}}, 
    datasets: [{
      label: 'Card Taps',
      data: {{analytics.counts}}
    }]
  }
});
</script>

✅ Tech Stack Suggestions

  • Express for routing

  • MongoDB or PostgreSQL

  • Handlebars for templating

  • Chart.js for analytics

  • Mongoose or Sequelize

  • Passport.js or custom auth middleware

🕒 3. Time-Based Redirect Destinations

Goal: Redirect to different URLs based on time of day (e.g., business hours vs personal site).

✅ How to Implement:

In your /tap/:cardUID route:

js
const hour = new Date().getHours();
let redirectTo = card.redirectUrl;

if (card.scheduleRedirects) {
  for (let rule of card.scheduleRedirects) {
    if (hour >= rule.startHour && hour < rule.endHour) {
      redirectTo = rule.url;
      break;
    }
  }
}

In the database, store card.scheduleRedirects like:

[

🗂 Data Model (Extended)

User

Card

🔨 Admin Dashboard Capabilities

Accessible via /admin, behind isAdmin middleware:

  • View all cards

  • Create and assign unique URLs (/tap/:cardUID)

  • Mark cards as “ready for activation”

  • Search/filter by status, user, UID

Example Route:

js
app.post('/admin/card/:cardUID/assign', isAdmin, async (req, res) => {
  const { userId, redirectUrl } = req.body;
  const card = await Card.findOne({ cardUID: req.params.cardUID });
  card.owner = userId;
  card.redirectUrl = redirectUrl;
  card.isActivated = false;
  await card.save();
  res.redirect('/admin');
});

👤 User Flow

  1. User logs in → Dashboard

    • See a list of unactivated cards assigned to them

  2. User activates a card

    • Visits /activate/:cardUID

    • If logged in and the card is assigned to them:

      • Can update profile info

      • Click "Activate"

      • Card is now live and redirectable

Activation Route:

js
app.get('/activate/:cardUID', isAuthenticated, async (req, res) => {
  const card = await Card.findOne({ cardUID: req.params.cardUID });

  if (!card || card.owner.toString() !== req.session.userID)
    return res.status(403).send('Unauthorized');

  if (card.isActivated) return res.redirect('/dashboard');

  res.render('activateCard', { card });
});

app.post('/activate/:cardUID', isAuthenticated, async (req, res) => {
  const card = await Card.findOne({ cardUID: req.params.cardUID });

  if (!card || card.owner.toString() !== req.session.userID)
    return res.status(403).send('Unauthorized');

  card.profile = {
    name: req.body.name,
    description: req.body.description,
    imageUrl: req.body.imageUrl
  };
  card.isActivated = true;
  await card.save();

  res.redirect('/dashboard');
});

📊 Tap & Analytics Flow

When someone visits /tap/:cardUID:

  1. Find card by UID.

  2. Log the tap (IP, timestamp, referrer, etc.).

  3. Redirect to card.redirectUrl.

Bonus: Use a background task or hook for geo-location (MaxMind or ipapi.co).

🌐 Routes

routes/tap.js

js
const express = require('express');
const router = express.Router();
const Card = require('../models/Card');
const Analytics = require('../models/Analytics');

router.get('/:cardUID', async (req, res) => {
  const card = await Card.findOne({ cardUID: req.params.cardUID });
  if (!card || !card.isActivated) return res.status(404).send('Not found');

  const hour = new Date().getHours();
  let redirectUrl = card.redirectUrl;

  if (card.scheduleRedirects) {
    for (let rule of card.scheduleRedirects) {
      if (hour >= rule.startHour && hour < rule.endHour) {
        redirectUrl = rule.url;
        break;
      }
    }
  }

  await Analytics.create({
    cardId: card._id,
    timestamp: new Date(),
    ipAddress: req.ip,
    userAgent: req.headers['user-agent'],
    referrer: req.headers['referer'] || '',
  });

  res.redirect(redirectUrl);
});

module.exports = router;

  const card = await Card.findOne({ cardUID: req.params.cardUID });

  if (!card || card.owner.toString() !== req.session.userID) {
    return res.status(403).send('Unauthorized');
  }

  res.render('activateCard', { card });
});

router.post('/:cardUID', isAuthenticated, async (req, res) => {
  const card = await Card.findOne({ cardUID: req.params.cardUID });

  if (!card || card.owner.toString() !== req.session.userID) {
    return res.status(403).send('Unauthorized');
  }

  card.profile = {
    name: req.body.name,
    description: req.body.description,
    imageUrl: req.body.imageUrl,
  };
  card.isActivated = true;
  await card.save();

  res.redirect('/dashboard');
});

module.exports = router;

👥 User Registration & Login

1. Dependencies

bash
npm install bcryptjs express-session

2. Auth Routes (routes/auth.js)

js
const express = require('express');
const bcrypt = require('bcryptjs');
const User = require('../models/User');
const router = express.Router();

// Register
router.get('/register', (req, res) => res.render('register'));

router.post('/register', async (req, res) => {
  const { email, password } = req.body;
  const passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash(password, 10);
  const user = new User({ email, passwordHash });
  await user.save();
  req.session.userID = user._id;
  req.session.userRole = user.role;
  res.redirect('/dashboard');
});

// Login
router.get('/login', (req, res) => res.render('login'));

router.post('/login', async (req, res) => {
  const user = await User.findOne({ email: req.body.email });
  if (user && await bcrypt.compare(req.body.password, user.passwordHash)) {
    req.session.userID = user._id;
    req.session.userRole = user.role;
    res.redirect('/dashboard');
  } else {
    res.render('login', { error: 'Invalid credentials' });
  }
});

// Logout
router.get('/logout', (req, res) => {
  req.session.destroy(() => res.redirect('/login'));
});

module.exports = router;

3. Add to app.js

js
app.use('/', require('./routes/auth'));

Let’s add another layer of functionality to make this platform even more powerful. Here's a breakdown of a few optional advanced features, and then we'll build out email summaries as an example:

🔧 Optional Feature Layers

  1. 📍 Location-Based Tap Logging
    Log geolocation data using IP-based services (e.g., ipapi, MaxMind, or geoip-lite) to show tap maps.

  2. 📬 Daily/Weekly Email Summaries
    Send users a digest of how many taps they got, which cards were most active, etc.

  3. 🔔 Webhook Callbacks
    Allow advanced users to set a webhook URL that gets POSTed to every time their card is tapped.

  4. 💡 Tap Heatmaps
    Aggregate most-tapped cards and present insights on “what’s hot.”

📬 Feature Focus: Daily/Weekly Email Summaries

1. Install Dependencies

bash
npm install nodemailer node-cron

2. Mailer Setup (utils/mailer.js)

js
const nodemailer = require('nodemailer');

const transporter = nodemailer.createTransport({
  service: 'gmail',
  auth: {
    user: process.env.EMAIL_USER,
    pass: process.env.EMAIL_PASS
  }
});

async function sendEmail(to, subject, html) {
  await transporter.sendMail({
    from: '"NFC Dashboard" <noreply@nfcapp.com>',
    to,
    subject,
    html
  });
}

module.exports = sendEmail;

3. Cron Job (cron/emailDigest.js)

js
const cron = require('node-cron');
const User = require('../models/User');
const Card = require('../models/Card');
const Analytics = require('../models/Analytics');
const sendEmail = require('../utils/mailer');

cron.schedule('0 8 * * *', async () => {
  const users = await User.find({});

  for (let user of users) {
    const cards = await Card.find({ owner: user._id });
    const cardIds = cards.map(c => c._id);

    const today = new Date();
    today.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);

    const tapCount = await Analytics.countDocuments({
      cardId: { $in: cardIds },
      timestamp: { $gte: today }
    });

    const html = `
      <h3>Your NFC Tap Summary</h3>
      <p>You had <b>${tapCount}</b> tap(s) on your cards today.</p>
      <a href="https://yourdashboard.com/dashboard">View Your Dashboard</a>
    `;

    if (tapCount > 0) {
      await sendEmail(user.email, '📈 Your NFC Card Activity for Today', html);
    }
  }

  console.log('Daily email summaries sent.');
});

4. Load the Cron Job in app.js

js
require('./cron/emailDigest');

📧 Self-Hosted Email Service

If you're not using a third-party email (like Gmail), here are two solid self-hosting options:

1. Mailu / Mailcow

  • Mailu: Lightweight Docker-based mail server with a nice admin UI.

  • Mailcow: More feature-rich, supports DKIM, SPF, SOGo webmail, etc.

  • Can run in a separate Portainer stack.

  • Use SMTP from your hosted mail domain (e.g., smtp.yourdomain.com) in nodemailer.

✅ Make sure your domain has correct DNS records: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and reverse DNS for clean email delivery.

  const card = await Card.findOne({ cardUID: req.params.cardUID });
  if (!card || !card.isActivated) return res.status(404).send('Not found');

  const ip = req.headers['x-forwarded-for'] || req.socket.remoteAddress;
  const geo = geoip.lookup(ip);

  await Analytics.create({
    cardId: card._id,
    timestamp: new Date(),
    ipAddress: ip,
    userAgent: req.headers['user-agent'],
    referrer: req.headers['referer'] || '',
    location: geo ? {
      city: geo.city,
      region: geo.region,
      country: geo.country,
      ll: geo.ll
    } : null
  });

  res.redirect(card.redirectUrl);
});

🧠 Backend Route Structure

/routes/dashboard.js

js
const express = require('express');
const router = express.Router();
const Card = require('../models/Card');
const Analytics = require('../models/Analytics');

router.get('/dashboard', isAuthenticated, async (req, res) => {
  const userId = req.session.userID;
  const cards = await Card.find({ owner: userId });

  const cardsWithAnalytics = await Promise.all(cards.map(async card => {
    const tapCount = await Analytics.countDocuments({ cardId: card._id });
    const lastTap = await Analytics.findOne({ cardId: card._id }).sort({ timestamp: -1 });

    return {
      _id: card._id,
      cardUID: card.cardUID,
      nickname: card.nickname,
      redirectUrl: card.redirectUrl,
      tapCount,
      lastTapFormatted: lastTap ? lastTap.timestamp.toLocaleString() : 'Never'
    };
  }));

  res.render('dashboard', {
    user: req.session.user,
    cards: cardsWithAnalytics
  });
});

  • Pulls all the user’s cards

  • Adds tap stats (count + latest)

  • Lists each card in a clean, styled card

Let's say a user wants to merge their cards to one profile, yet with each card it's individual links. ChatGPT said:

To achieve this functionality, you'd want to create a card group feature. In this setup, the user would have the ability to:

  • Order multiple NFC cards, each with a unique link, but all cards are associated with a single profile.

  • The profile dictates where the group of cards redirects to.

  • When the user updates the profile (e.g., changes the redirect URL), it affects all cards associated with that profile.

Here’s how you can structure this:

Database Design Changes

You'll need two main changes to the database:

  1. Profile: A user can have multiple NFC cards, but all cards will point to a shared profile.

  2. Card: Each card will be associated with a profile, and the card's unique identifier will still keep its unique link for tracking purposes.

Database Schema Example

1. Profile Schema

js
const mongoose = require('mongoose');

const profileSchema = new mongoose.Schema({
  userId: { type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'User' },
  nickname: String,
  redirectUrl: String, // The URL that this profile points to
  webhookUrl: String, // Optional
  cards: [{ type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'Card' }],
  timeBasedRedirects: [{
    from: String,
    to: String,
    url: String,
  }],
  notifications: {
    email: { type: Boolean, default: false },
    sms: { type: Boolean, default: false },
  },
});

const Profile = mongoose.model('Profile', profileSchema);
module.exports = Profile;

2. Card Schema

js
const mongoose = require('mongoose');

const cardSchema = new mongoose.Schema({
  cardUID: String, // Unique card identifier
  owner: { type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'User' },
  profile: { type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'Profile' }, // Link to the profile
  tapCount: { type: Number, default: 0 },
  lastTapped: Date,
});

const Card = mongoose.model('Card', cardSchema);
module.exports = Card;

Frontend Flow

  1. Order 10 Cards: When a customer orders 10 cards, they are each assigned a unique cardUID but are linked to the same Profile in the database.

  2. Single Profile: The profile has one redirect URL that is applied across all the cards. The customer can modify the redirect URL, and it updates all linked cards.

  3. Edit Profile: The user can go to their profile settings and update things like:

    • Main redirect URL

    • Time-based redirects

    • Webhook URL

    • Notification settings

Backend Flow (Edit Profile)

  1. The user edits their Profile with changes like the redirect URL or webhook.

  2. The backend updates the Profile model and reflects the changes for all associated Cards.

Profile Update Route (Express)

js
const express = require('express');
const router = express.Router();
const Profile = require('../models/Profile');
const Card = require('../models/Card');

router.post('/profile/:id/edit', isAuthenticated, async (req, res) => {
  const { id } = req.params;
  const { nickname, redirectUrl, webhookUrl, notifications, timeBasedRedirects } = req.body;

  // Update profile
  const profile = await Profile.findById(id);
  if (!profile) {
    return res.status(404).send('Profile not found');
  }

  profile.nickname = nickname;
  profile.redirectUrl = redirectUrl;
  profile.webhookUrl = webhookUrl;
  profile.notifications = notifications;
  profile.timeBasedRedirects = timeBasedRedirects;

  await profile.save();

  // Update all associated cards' redirects
  await Card.updateMany({ profile: profile._id }, { $set: { redirectUrl: profile.redirectUrl } });

  res.redirect('/dashboard');
});

Workflow Recap:

  1. User orders 10 cards -> each card has a unique cardUID, but they share the same Profile.

  2. Profile dictates redirects — update one Profile URL, and it updates all associated cards' URLs.

  3. Edit Profile settings — tweak URL, time-based redirects, webhook, and notifications for all cards in that profile.

Additional Notes:

  • The Profile links to Cards via a profile field in the Card schema.

  • The Cards are all updated when changes are made to the Profile.

  • Optionally, you could give users the ability to unlink individual cards from the profile, but keeping the system as a group simplifies management.

1. app.js (Main Server Setup)

js
require('dotenv').config();
const express = require('express');
const session = require('express-session');
const mongoose = require('mongoose');
const handlebars = require('express-handlebars');
const passport = require('passport');
const app = express();

// Middleware setup
app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true }));
app.use(express.json());
app.use(session({ secret: 'secret', resave: false, saveUninitialized: true }));
app.use(passport.initialize());
app.use(passport.session());

// Handlebars Setup
app.engine('hbs', handlebars({ extname: 'hbs', defaultLayout: 'main' }));
app.set('view engine', 'hbs');

// Database Connection
mongoose.connect(process.env.DB_URI, { useNewUrlParser: true, useUnifiedTopology: true })
  .then(() => console.log('MongoDB connected'))
  .catch(err => console.log(err));

// Routes
const dashboardRoutes = require('./routes/dashboard');
const profileRoutes = require('./routes/profile');
const cardRoutes = require('./routes/card');
const authRoutes = require('./routes/auth');

app.use('/dashboard', dashboardRoutes);
app.use('/profile', profileRoutes);
app.use('/card', cardRoutes);
app.use('/auth', authRoutes);

// Home Route
app.get('/', (req, res) => {
  res.render('index');
});

// Start Server
const PORT = process.env.PORT || 3000;
app.listen(PORT, () => console.log(`Server running on port ${PORT}`));

const express = require('express');

const isAuthenticated = require('../middleware/auth');

// Edit Profile Route
router.get('/:id/edit', isAuthenticated, async (req, res) => {
  const profile = await Profile.findById(req.params.id);
  res.render('profile-edit', { profile });
});

router.post('/:id/edit', isAuthenticated, async (req, res) => {
  const { nickname, redirectUrl, webhookUrl, notifications } = req.body;
  const profile = await Profile.findByIdAndUpdate(req.params.id, { nickname, redirectUrl, webhookUrl, notifications });

  // Update all cards associated with this profile
  await Card.updateMany({ profile: profile._id }, { $set: { redirectUrl: profile.redirectUrl } });

  res.redirect('/dashboard');
});

module.exports = router;

# NFC Card Dashboard

This is an NFC card management dashboard where users can manage their NFC cards, update redirects, view analytics, and receive notifications.

## Features

- **User Authentication**: Register and log in to access your NFC cards.
- **Card Management**: View and edit card settings (redirect URL, time-based redirects).
- **Analytics**: View tap history, charts, and geo-location map for each card.
- **Notifications**: Set up email/SMS alerts on each card's tap events.
- **Twilio Integration**: Premium users can receive SMS alerts on taps.

## Installation

1. Clone the repo:

git clone https://github.com/yourusername/nfc-card-dashboard.git cd nfc-card-dashboard

markdown

2. Install dependencies:

npm install

markdown

3. Create a `.env` file:

DB_URI=mongodb://localhost/nfc-dashboard TWILIO_SID=your_twilio_sid TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN=your_twilio_auth_token TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER=your_twilio_phone_number

markdown

4. Start the server:

npm start

bash

## Routes

- `/dashboard`: User dashboard where they can manage NFC cards.
- `/profile/:id/edit`: Edit profile settings (e.g., redirect URLs).
- `/card/:id/edit`: Edit card-specific settings.
